learningObjectives: Use custom TCP references in API values.
Navigate to referenced Modules and add TestSteps using current commands.
Distinguish hidden empty actions from empty values.
Update changed Modules and their mappings before targeted verification.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Build an independently specified API flow

elements.text: Independent example: create a disposable resource, buffer its returned identifier, retrieve that resource and assert expected fields, then delete it where permitted. Do not assume every service uses a list Constraint or the same cleanup semantics. A passing run needs all required assertions, not just successful transport.

Create a custom TCP on a supported TestCase/folder or other configuration-bearing object, and reference it in values with {CP[Key]}. Child objects inherit the value; lower-level overrides apply. Do not create a separate TCP on every TestStepValue. Use the appropriate supported data type, including Password where suitable, and follow your project credential-handling policy.
Use TestStep context menu > Jump to Module or Ctrl+Shift+J to inspect the linked Module. Drag a Module onto a TestCase or use Ctrl+T to launch Search and Add TestStep; choose the intended result.

F9 controls show/hide context-sensitive objects, including DoNothing. The View menu hides steps/values with an empty ActionMode; this is not the same as hiding every empty Value, and hiding does not repair missing input.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Refresh selected Modules and inspect affected mappings

elements.text: Open the affected Module through API Testing > API Scan > Open selected Modules, edit the message and click Update. Review each changed request/response Module; do not assume selecting only one refreshes all related artifacts.

Changed element mappings may require ModuleAttribute Update and Validate. Corresponding message updates do not guarantee every expected value, XPath or business assertion is correct. Inspect affected TestSteps and execute targeted tests.

Check inputs, credential references, returned identity, assertions, mapping validity and cleanup. A WorkState label is workflow metadata rather than proof of exhaustive validation. Original Academy slides and end-to-end exercise execution have not been verified.

examPitfalls.title: Using an outdated navigation shortcut
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Relying on the former Ctrl+J claim.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use Jump to Module or current Ctrl+Shift+J.

examPitfalls.title: Defining configuration on every value
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Repeating the same custom TCP definition everywhere.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Define it on a supported object and reference it via {CP[name]}.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming one update repairs all relationships
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Ignoring changed mappings or a separately changed response.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect affected Modules, update mappings and validate.

examPitfalls.title: Treating Ctrl+T as an immediate insert
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the first search result is automatically the right Module.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Ctrl+T launches Fuzzy Search; choose the intended result.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which current command navigates from a TestStep to its referenced Module?

options.text: Jump to Module in the context menu, or Ctrl+Shift+J.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Current Commander documentation names this command and shortcut.

optionExplanations.A: Manual search is unnecessary when a reference exists.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What shortcut controls contextual show/hide, including DoNothing objects?
practiceQuiz.hint: DoNothing concerns empty actions, not merely empty values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: F9 is the current show/hide shortcut; inspect context and ActionMode.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you refresh an existing API Module after its message changes?

options.text: Open the selected Module in API Scan, modify the message and click Update; inspect changed attribute mappings too.
Save the workspace and assume every server change is detected.

practiceQuiz.hint: The message and mapping updates have different scopes.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Scan Update refreshes the corresponding Module; changed attributes also need inspection.

optionExplanations.A: A complete rebuild is not mandatory.
optionExplanations.B: This follows the update workflow and addresses mapping risk.
optionExplanations.C: Saving is not automatic server change discovery.
optionExplanations.D: Renaming does not perform a rescan.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A request Module and a separate response Module both need message changes. What scope should be reviewed?

options.text: Both affected Modules, with their mappings and TestSteps inspected.
Every unrelated Module must be deleted.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Each affected Module needs review; do not assume one-side updates cover all changes.

optionExplanations.A: The changed request would be missed.
optionExplanations.B: The changed response would be missed.
optionExplanations.C: This includes both changed artifacts and their mappings.
optionExplanations.D: Unrelated Modules do not require deletion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can a Module be added as a TestStep?

options.text: Drag it onto a TestCase, or use Ctrl+T and choose it in Search and Add TestStep.
Only a special Insert API Module command.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Both drag-and-drop and Fuzzy Search support creating TestSteps.

optionExplanations.C: That exclusive command is not the documented requirement.

quickRecap.value: Inspect the linked Module; do not equate refreshed messages with validated assertions.
Context menu Jump to Module or Ctrl+Shift+J.
Define on a supported object and reference {CP[name]}.
Empty ActionMode; not synonymous with empty Value.
Update and validate each affected attribute; execute assertions.
Drag Module or Ctrl+T, then choose a search result.
